result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A opens with the decision and its consequence, and gives every page a full-sentence takeaway title backed by figures and labels, so each page reads well on its own. B also puts the decision early, on the title and summary slides, but uses topic-only titles and has very thin slides (Lease Rates, Distribution) that look built for a presenter. Both keep to the supplied figures plus arithmetic and flag the derived numbers and the Saturday deadline. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B opens with the decision and its consequence, and every slide title is a full-sentence takeaway, so each page makes sense when read alone. A also flags the decision early, on its title and summary slides, but several of its slides are thin (the distribution slide is a single number, and the lease-rate slide repeats occupancy) and the full decision table only appears at the end. Both derive the drop to about 84% occupancy and say it is their own arithmetic; A additionally assumes the prior quarter is 'Q2 2026'.
